boundary: Scope: tekmerion.connectors.CoreConnector and its consumption by tekmerion.verification. CORE outputs/entities endpoints are out of scope (works only).

evidence.ref: src/tekmerion/connectors.py (the existing interface: search/resolve returning RetrievedItem; Crossref + OpenAlex as the pattern)

falsification_tests: F-012-1: any CORE-produced item reaching a CitationResult or evidence item with a source value other than "core", a result field outside the existing CitationResult shape, or a resolution/agreement/content value outside the vocabularies defined in tekmerion.verification.
claims.text: CORE results enter the pipeline through the same connector interface and outcome vocabulary as Crossref and OpenAlex: search/resolve return RetrievedItem records, resolution resolves to resolved / not_found / error, agreement and content use the existing stage vocabularies, and every CORE-produced item carries source="core". No parallel semantics, result type, or vocabulary exists for CORE anywhere in the pipeline.

boundary: Scope: grouping key 1 (same DOI / source-native ID) as implemented in verification.assign_origin_groups. Records without a DOI cannot fold by DOI and are outside this claim.

evidence.ref: specs/012-core-connector/spec.md (identity: source_id is the DOI; grouping key 1 folds by DOI)
src/tekmerion/verification.py::assign_origin_groups (key 1: cited DOI or resolved source_id, normalized)

falsification_tests: F-012-2: a pipeline run in which two citations of the same DOI, one resolved via Crossref/OpenAlex and one via CORE (as resolver or enricher), land in different origin groups, or a claim's independent-mass accounting counts the same DOI twice.
claims.text: A CORE record of a work is the same origin as a Crossref or OpenAlex record of the same work: origin grouping folds citations of the same DOI into one origin group regardless of which connector resolved or enriched each citation, so a work found in two sources is never double-counted as independent evidence.

boundary: Scope: content carried on the v3 record itself. Rights in the underlying repository deposit beyond what the record asserts are not adjudicated here; the rule is the program's standing one (no asserted licence, no content reuse), identical to Crossref's.

evidence.ref: docs/architecture/01-source-layer.md (WS1 registry: aggregated content carries per-work licences — "in CORE" is not redistributable)
src/tekmerion/connectors.py::CrossrefConnector._item (the precedent: abstract dropped when no licence is asserted; Crossref abstracts are not CC0)

falsification_tests: F-012-3: a CORE item whose abstract or full text reaches a stance check while its record asserted no licence; or a CORE item with an empty license_basis; or an NC-licensed CORE item with hosted_ok=True.
claims.text: Every CORE-sourced item carries its per-record licence basis, and CORE content (abstract or full text) is used for stance checks only where the record asserts a licence: a record asserting no licence has its content dropped at the connector and degrades to a metadata record with the basis — core-aggregated (no per-work licence asserted) — visible on the item; the degradation is never silent. Non-commercial licences mark the item hosted_ok=False under the existing RT2-1 rule.

boundary: Scope: tekmerion.connectors.CoreConnector status translation and verification._resolve's handling of a raising connector, on both the primary and enrichment paths.

evidence.ref: src/tekmerion/verification.py::_resolve (a raising connector is recorded and yields the error outcome when nothing resolved — the shape CORE plugs into)

falsification_tests: F-012-4: a fixture or live run in which a CORE 401/403/429/5xx or transport failure produces a not_found outcome for a citation no other connector resolved; or an enrichment-path CORE failure changes a resolved citation's outcome to error or not_found.
claims.text: CORE failures are reported in the existing outcome shapes, distinctly: a DOI the API answers 404 for is not_found; an auth failure (401/403), a rate limit (429), a server error, or a transport failure on the only remaining route is an error outcome — never not_found. A CORE failure during enrichment never un-resolves a citation another connector resolved: the primary record stands and the failure is noted in the result detail.

boundary: Scope: CoreConnector's budget use and the spec/assessment records' accounting language. The external token ceiling of the owner's key tier (1,000 tokens/day) is CORE's, enforced by CORE; the CreditBudget limit is local configuration as elsewhere.

evidence.ref: specs/012-core-connector/spec.md (budget accounting section: token metering, no published per-call price)
specs/002-mvp-implementation/evaluation/EVALUATION-REPORT.md §4.5 + §2.5 (budget units are not dollars; price only from published rates — the lesson this accounting follows)

falsification_tests: F-012-5: a CORE HTTP call observed with no prior budget reservation; a call made after budget exhaustion; or any program record stating a dollar cost for CORE calls.
claims.text: Every CORE call is accounted before it happens: the connector reserves against a CreditBudget (search at the search rate, resolve at the get rate) and budget exhaustion raises before any HTTP call. Spend is reported in calls and budget units only: CORE publishes no per-call dollar price (the API is free with a registered key and metered in tokens — published tiers: 100 tokens/day unauthenticated, 1,000 tokens/day registered personal), so no dollar figure is ever attached to CORE usage.

boundary: Scope: verification._resolve ordering and the enrichment trigger. The no-DOI search path follows the same source order under the existing first-agreeing-candidate rule.

evidence.ref: specs/012-core-connector/spec.md (resolution order and enrichment: the integration decision and its rationale)
specs/002-mvp-implementation/evaluation/EVALUATION-REPORT.md §2.1 (the Phase 7 resolution-order reasoning this decision conserves)

falsification_tests: F-012-6: a fixture run in which a content-bearing primary resolution is followed by any CORE call, or produces an outcome differing in any field from the same run without CORE in the connector list.
claims.text: Resolution order is Crossref, then OpenAlex, then CORE, and CORE changes nothing for records the existing connectors already serve with content: when the primary resolution carries licence-permitted content, CORE is never called and the citation's outcome is identical to the pre-CORE pipeline. CORE acts as primary resolver only where the earlier connectors do not resolve, and as enricher only where the primary record has no licence-permitted content.

boundary: Scope: DOI-bearing citations whose primary record lacks licence-permitted content. When CORE serves full text but no abstract, the stance check runs on the full text and inherits the lexical checker's recorded sentence-level brittleness (Phase 7 §4.2) — the outcome is a checked-stage instrument reading, labeled by the extractor identity as always.

evidence.ref: specs/012-core-connector/spec.md (why CORE, and why now: the RT-5 dilution measured on CIT-E-302)
specs/002-mvp-implementation/evaluation/EVALUATION-REPORT.md §2.3/§2.1 (CLM-E-003's inconclusive by interval dilution against Schuch's metadata-only record, DOI 10.1016/j.jpsychires.2016.02.023)
docs/architecture/01-source-layer.md (WS1 registry: CORE = content channel for WS5 §1.3 content checks, "full-text aggregation where rights permit")

falsification_tests: F-012-7: a fixture or live case in which the primary record is contentless, CORE serves the same DOI with licence-permitted content that stage 2 accepts, and the citation still exits metadata_only; or an enrichment substitution where the CORE candidate disagrees with the citation on a stage-2 field.
claims.text: A record that is metadata-only at Crossref and OpenAlex but carries licence-permitted content at CORE is content-checked, not metadata-only: the enrichment path returns the CORE record for the same DOI (stage 2 in agreement), and the citation's content outcome is the stance check's verdict on that content instead of the RT-5 metadata-only dilution.

boundary: Scope: tekmerion.mcp.server._default_connectors. Other assemblies (UI callers, evaluation drivers) pass explicit connector lists as today; their documented order is Crossref, OpenAlex, CORE.

evidence.ref: src/tekmerion/mcp/server.py::_default_connectors (the OpenAlex key-gated append pattern CORE follows)

falsification_tests: F-012-8: a server started without CORE_API_KEY that errors, warns fatally, or assembles a CoreConnector; or a server started with the key whose default list lacks CORE or places it before an existing connector.
claims.text: The MCP server's default connector assembly includes CORE exactly when CORE_API_KEY is present in the server environment — appended after Crossref and OpenAlex — and omits it silently when the key is absent, so a deployment without a CORE key behaves byte-identically to today and never fails at startup over a missing optional key.
